invariants.why: a fixed lookAt(0,0,0) threw the view back to the origin on every turn after a pan; the target is what keeps the user's place
pan is defined in the view plane by the matrix columns; moving in the ground plane instead is the classic OrbitControls mistake
pan and anchored zoom read those columns; without forcing the update the first drag after a turn uses the previous view's axes
additive zoom steps are huge near the minimum and imperceptible near the maximum, which is what made the wheel feel stuck at one end
a fixed per-frame lerp makes the same gesture frame-rate dependent: slow at 60 Hz, frantic at 144 Hz

invariants.must_contain: current** zoom, not the target zoom
invariants.why: the anchor must hold the point that is on screen now, not the one the animation is heading toward
the integer-zoom rule came from the removed PixiJS 2D stage; restating it as live would forbid the fluid zoom for a reason that no longer applies
the true-isometric angle vs the 2:1 dimetric 30 degrees is the number that keeps the look consistent with the sprite projection
lerping positions cuts through the inside of the circle and swings the camera closer to the map mid-turn
